construction_markdown:
No new code is claimed. Start with the verifier-accepted RS–affine `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2` handoff. Write its generator columns as `z_v∈V=F_2^1040`. Because this code contains the all-one word, there is a nonzero functional `x_0∈V*` satisfying `x_0(z_v)=1` for every base coordinate `v`.

A replacement-product or parity-walk lift selects exactly `n=2^30` finite sequences `p` of base coordinates and outputs the columns `g_p=⊕_{v∈p}z_v`. The proposed route would use these columns as a 1040-dimensional balanced core and append an independent all-one row, producing dimension 1041.

This turn proves an exact criterion for that route. Choose one base column `z_*` and put `H=ker(x_0)`. Separate paths according to the parity of their number of summands. For `ψ∈H*`, define

`E_ψ=Σ_{p even}(-1)^{ψ(g_p)}` and `O_ψ=Σ_{p odd}(-1)^{ψ(g_p+z_*)}`.

The all-one augmentation meets the target exactly when the two parity classes differ in size by at most `2^21` and `|E_ψ|+|O_ψ|≤2^21` for every nonzero `ψ`. Thus opposite-parity cancellation cannot supply the missing estimate: the paired characters `ψ` and `ψ+x_0` force the sum of the two absolute correlations.

The criterion leaves a sharply defined but unresolved gateway: construct two deterministic, non-paired path families of near-equal size satisfying the simultaneous quotient-character bound. Fixed-parity lifts, naive parity toggles of one quotient multiset, and mixtures certified only by published complete-cloud absolute bounds do not pass this gateway.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Conditional transformation only. Fix the accepted RS–affine base matrix with rows indexed by `(i,j)∈{0,…,15}×{0,…,64}` and base entry at `v=(a,y)` equal to `H(α^i a^j)_y`, where `α=Z` in `F_2[Z]/(Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1)`. Given a deterministic indexer `Path:{0,1}^30→` finite lists of base coordinates, emit `G[(i,j),q]=⊕_{v∈Path(q)}H(α^i a_v^j)_{y_v}` for all 1040 rows and all `q`, followed by one all-one row. No concrete qualifying `Path` is asserted here.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: If every path has at most `L(n)≤n^c` entries and the indexer takes at most `n^c` bit operations per output for a fixed integer `c`, the full matrix is emitted in `O(1040·n^(c+1)+1040n)` bit operations, hence `n^{O(1)}`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: The base matrix can be precomputed in `O(1040n)` fixed-degree field operations. There are exactly `1040n` lifted core entries, and each is an XOR of at most `n^c` precomputed bits. The path descriptions take at most `n·n^c` additional work. Finally, exactly `n` constant-row bits are emitted.

proof_markdown:
### 1. Fourier formulation

Let `V=F_2^1040`, and let `z_v∈V` be the columns of the accepted RS–affine generator matrix. Its all-one message is a nonzero `x_0∈V*` with `x_0(z_v)=1` for every `v`. For a path descriptor `p`, put `g_p=⊕_{v∈p}z_v`. Hence

`x_0(g_p)=|p| mod 2`.

For any `χ∈V*`, the corresponding lifted word has signed sum

`S_χ=Σ_p(-1)^{χ(g_p)}`

and weight `(n−S_χ)/2`. After adjoining an all-one row, both this word and its complement occur. They both have weight at least `D` exactly when `|S_χ|≤n−2D=T`.

### 2. Exact parity split

Fix a base column `z_*`; then `x_0(z_*)=1`. Put `H=ker x_0`, and partition the path multiset into `Q_0,Q_1` by even and odd parity. Thus `g_p∈H` on `Q_0`, while `g_p+z_*∈H` on `Q_1`.

Given `ψ∈H*`, take its unique extension `χ` to `V` satisfying `χ(z_*)=0`. Its other extension is `χ+x_0`. Define

`E_ψ=Σ_{p∈Q_0}(-1)^{ψ(g_p)}`,
`O_ψ=Σ_{p∈Q_1}(-1)^{ψ(g_p+z_*)}`.

The two extension sums are respectively `E_ψ+O_ψ` and `E_ψ−O_ψ`. For real numbers `E,O`,

`max{|E+O|,|E−O|}=|E|+|O|`.

For `ψ=0`, the zero extension is irrelevant and the nonzero extension `x_0` gives `|Q_0|−|Q_1|`. For every nonzero `ψ`, both extensions are nonzero. Consequently all nonzero characters satisfy `|S_χ|≤T` if and only if

`||Q_0|−|Q_1||≤T`

and

`|E_ψ|+|O_ψ|≤T` for every `0≠ψ∈H*`.

This proves the criterion and shows why opposite-parity cancellation cannot help: switching from `χ` to `χ+x_0` reverses only the odd contribution.

### 3. Dimension, distance, and parity sizes

Because `T<n`, the criterion forces `{g_p}` to span `V`; otherwise a nonzero annihilating character would have signed sum `n`. It also excludes all-one from the lifted core, since such a core word would have signed sum `−n`. The core therefore has dimension 1040 and adjoining all-one adds an independent dimension. Every nonzero augmented word is either a core word, its complement, or all-one, so its weight is at least `(n−T)/2=D`.

The parity-size inequality and `|Q_0|+|Q_1|=n` give

`2^29−2^20≤|Q_i|≤2^29+2^20`.

Also `|E_ψ|,|O_ψ|≤T`, so each parity class individually must have normalized quotient bias at most `T/(2^29−2^20)=2/511`.

All-even paths have columns in `H` and rank at most 1039. All-odd paths make `x_0` the all-one core word. Thus neither fixed parity can yield the required balanced rank-1040 core.

### 4. Paired-toggle reduction

Consider the symmetric repair formed from a multiset `{h_q:q=1,…,2^29}⊂H`: output one even column `h_q` and one odd column `h_q+z_*` for every `q`. Then the parity classes have equal size and

`E_ψ=O_ψ=W_ψ:=Σ_q(-1)^{ψ(h_q)}`.

The exact criterion becomes `|W_ψ|≤2^20` for every nonzero `ψ`. Therefore the repair already requires a rank-1039, length-`2^29`, `1/512`-balanced multiset. It does not amplify bias.

Within the ordinary RS–affine family at this half length, let the field degree be `a`. The inner affine table has length `2^(a−1)`, so the evaluation set must have size `N=2^(30−a)`. Alphabet feasibility gives `a≥15`. A degree-`t` polynomial has at most `t` roots, and the distance condition is

`(N−t)2^(a−2)≥2^28−2^19`,

hence `t≤floor(2^(21−a))`. The full dimensions for `a=15,…,21` are `975,528,289,162,95,60,42`; for `a≥22` they are at most 30. The maximum is 975. Removing the all-one direction gives balanced rank 974; parity toggling restores one direction and final all-one augmentation adds one more, for only 976 dimensions.

### 5. Complete-cloud stitching obstruction

Suppose each parity distribution is a disjoint union of complete clouds, each using a quotient base-label set spanning all 1039 dimensions, and suppose the proof combines published component bounds by triangle inequality. If component `i` has length `M_i` and certified normalized bound `b_i`, the resulting certificate is at least `Σ_i b_iM_i`. Since `Σ_iM_i=n>T`, such a proof requires some `b_i<1`.

For a complete Ta-Shma component with full quotient span, the published finite trace audit says `b_i<1` forces `M_i≥2^30+2^24>n`, impossible inside the disjoint union.

For a complete Gray-register component, `b_i<1` forces register length at least 3 and inner normalized eigenvalue below `1/2`. Compatibility gives outer eigenvalue below `1/40`. The trace inequality on 1039 outer vertices then gives degree `d≥631`; double-conflict-freeness gives width at least 3, and the inner trace inequality gives degree at least 4. Thus

`M_i≥1039·631^3·4^3=16706427843136>n`.

Hence componentwise stitching of these complete clouds cannot prove the parity criterion. This conclusion deliberately does not cover cancellations analyzed jointly across components or sparse, non-Cartesian path sets.

theorem_statement: For the accepted 1040-dimensional affine-hyperplane base, a length-`2^30` XOR-path lift becomes a target-qualified dimension-1041 code after adjoining all-one if and only if its even and odd path classes satisfy `||Q_0|−|Q_1||≤2^21` and `|E_ψ|+|O_ψ|≤2^21` for every nonzero character of the 1039-dimensional quotient hyperplane. Consequently fixed parity fails, identical parity toggling merely reduces to a length-`2^29` rank-1039 `1/512`-bias problem, and published absolute bounds for unmodified full-rank complete Ta-Shma or Gray clouds cannot be combined componentwise to prove the criterion. No qualifying mixed-parity family is currently supplied.
